# Algeria Compass

> Algeria Compass is a licensed Algerian tour operator running private, expert-guided
> cultural, Sahara and luxury journeys across Algeria, with visa support and local
> Algerian guides. We also publish independent, fact-checked travel guides on visiting
> Algeria — safety, visas, transport, costs, seasons, food and its seven UNESCO World
> Heritage sites. Guides are written by Oussama Ben Yahia (founder) and independently
> reviewed against our published editorial standards.
> Languages served: Arabic, Tamazight, French, English, Spanish, Italian.
> Contact: https://algeriacompass.com/contact/

## Travel guides (independent, fact-checked)
- [20 Best Things to Do in Algeria (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/things-to-do-in-algeria/): From the best-preserved Roman cities on earth to the sand seas of the Tassili, the Casbah of Algiers and the oasis towns of the M'Zab — the essential things to see and do across Algeria.
- [Algeria Itinerary: How to Plan 7, 10 & 14 Days (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-itinerary/): How many days do you need in Algeria, and what should you actually see? Ready-made 7, 10 and 14-day itineraries — north, coast and Sahara — with the routes, seasons and logistics that make them work.
- [Algeria Packing List: What to Bring (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-packing-list/): What to pack for Algeria — for the northern cities, the coast and the Sahara. Clothing, documents, cash, medications and the desert-specific kit that trips people up.
- [Algeria Visa Guide (2026): Types, Documents, Process](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-visa-guide/): Who needs a visa for Algeria, which type to apply for, the documents and fees involved, processing times, the special case of the far-south desert, and how to avoid the common reasons for refusal.
- [Algeria vs Morocco: Which to Visit? (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-vs-morocco/): Algeria or Morocco? An honest comparison for travellers — crowds, cost, ease, Sahara, Roman heritage and food — to help you choose the right North African trip.
- [Algeria vs Tunisia: Which to Visit? (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-vs-tunisia/): Algeria or Tunisia? An honest comparison of two North African neighbours — ease, cost, beaches, Roman ruins, Sahara and crowds — to help you pick the right trip.
- [Algeria with Kids: Family Travel Guide (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-family-travel/): Is Algeria good for families? What works with children — the coast, Roman cities and oasis towns — what to skip, and the practicalities of food, health, transport and hotels.
- [Algerian Food: A Traveller's Guide to Couscous, Tagines and Mint Tea](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algerian-food-guide/): Algerian cooking sits at a crossroads of Amazigh, Arab, Ottoman, Andalusian and French influences. Here are the dishes to seek out.
- [Algerian Handicrafts: Pottery, Brass and the Desert Craft Markets](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algerian-handicrafts/): From turquoise M'Zab pottery to engraved brass and woven baskets, Algeria's craft traditions are alive and affordable.
- [Algerian Sahara Travel Guide: Djanet, Timimoun and the Tadrart](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algerian-sahara-travel-guide/): Algeria holds the largest slice of the Sahara of any country on earth — and almost no crowds. Here is how to actually experience it.
- [Christmas & New Year in Algeria: A Warm Winter Escape](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/christmas-new-year-in-algeria/): Spend Christmas and New Year in Algeria: the Sahara is in its prime season, the coast is mild, the mountains have snow — and there are no festive crowds or holiday price surges.
- [Getting Around Algeria: The Complete Transportation Guide](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-transportation-guide/): How to move around Africa's largest country: domestic flights, trains, buses, shared taxis, trams, private drivers and desert 4x4 — with routes, travel times, costs and booking advice.
- [How Much Does a Trip to Algeria Cost? (2026 Budget Guide)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-travel-cost/): Is Algeria expensive? A clear, current breakdown of what a trip really costs — accommodation, food, transport, guides and the Sahara — plus the dual exchange rate that changes everything on the ground.
- [Is Algeria Safe in 2026? An Evidence-Based Guide](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-safety-guide/): A calm, evidence-based look at safety in Algeria: crime, road and desert risks, women and family travel, regional differences, scams, emergencies and what official advisories actually say.
- [Ramadan, Eid & Holidays in Algeria: A Traveller's Guide](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-holidays-ramadan/): How Algeria's religious and national holidays affect travel — Ramadan, the two Eids, Mawlid and Ashura, plus Yennayer and Independence Day, and what Christmas and Easter look like in a majority-Muslim country.
- [SIM Cards & Internet in Algeria: Staying Connected (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-sim-internet/): How to get online in Algeria — local SIM cards, the three networks, data prices, eSIM and roaming, Wi-Fi reality, and what actually works in the Sahara.
- [Snow to Sahara: Four Seasons in One Algeria Trip](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/algeria-snow-to-sahara/): Does it snow in Algeria? Yes — and you can stand in cedar-forest snow and warm Saharan dunes in the same week. How to build a trip that spans the country's climates.
- [Solo Female Travel in Algeria: Is It Safe? (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/solo-female-travel-algeria/): An honest guide to solo female travel in Algeria — safety, dress, harassment, the north vs the Sahara, and practical tips for travelling well as a woman.
- [The Best Time to Visit Algeria: A Month-by-Month Guide](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/best-time-to-visit-algeria/): Algeria has three climates at once. This month-by-month and region-by-region guide shows exactly when to go for the coast, the cities, the mountains and the Sahara — and which months to avoid.
- [The Complete Algeria Travel Guide (2026)](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/complete-algeria-travel-guide/): Africa's largest country, from the Mediterranean coast to the deep Sahara: when to go, how to get in and around, what it costs, and how to plan a first trip with confidence.
- [The M'Zab Valley: The Desert Cities That Astonished Le Corbusier](https://algeriacompass.com/blog/mzab-valley-le-corbusier/): Five fortified desert cities and an 11th-century blueprint for living — an urban design so radical Le Corbusier kept coming back to study it.

- [Djémila (Cuicul)](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/djemila/): Djémila, ancient Cuicul, is one of the best-preserved Roman cities in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1982. Set on a mountain spur in
- [M'Zab Valley](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/mzab-valley/): The M'Zab Valley around Ghardaïa is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the northern Algerian Sahara — five fortified oasis towns built by the Ibadi Mozab
- [Tassili n'Ajjer](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/tassili-najjer/): Tassili n'Ajjer is a vast sandstone plateau in south-east Algeria, a UNESCO World Heritage Site holding around 15,000 prehistoric engravings and paint
- [The Casbah of Algiers](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/casbah-of-algiers/): The Casbah of Algiers is the city's historic Ottoman citadel and old town — a steep maze of whitewashed houses, palaces, mosques and covered lanes ove
- [Timgad](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/timgad/): Timgad (ancient Thamugadi) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Batna state, eastern Algeria — a Roman colony founded around 100 AD by Trajan and the mo
- [Tipaza](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/tipaza/): Tipaza is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on the Mediterranean coast about 70 km west of Algiers — a Phoenician trading post that became an important Rom
- [Tlemcen](https://algeriacompass.com/destinations/tlemcen/): Tlemcen is a historic city in north-west Algeria, the country's great centre of Andalusian and Islamic heritage — the medieval Zayyanid capital famous
